identity.title: Context-dependent regulation and multidomain dynamics of HLTF.

content.abstract: The helicase-like transcription factor (HLTF) is a superfamily 2 translocase vital for maintaining genome integrity. As we discuss in this review article, recent breakthroughs show that HLTF alters its oligomeric state depending on substrate configuration, allowing it to coordinate mechanical DNA repair with epigenetic silencing. By anchoring its N-terminal HIP116 and Rad5 N-terminal domain directly onto exposed 3'-hydroxyl single-stranded DNA ends, HLTF operates as a monomer during nucleotide excision repair and post-cleavage CRISPR-associated protein 9 eviction to clear persistent protein roadblocks. Conversely, replication fork stress could promote self-assembly into an asymmetric homodimer to drive fork regression. Beyond physical DNA processing, HLTF resolves toxic G-quadruplex structures and stabilizes heterochromatin through its histone 3 lysine 23 ubiquitin ligase activity, exposing a targetable synthetic-lethal vulnerability in checkpoint-deficient tumors.
